newsitem.title: USA: Mass. Rep Kennedy wants FCC to probe liquor ads.
newsitem.headline: Mass. Rep Kennedy wants FCC to probe liquor ads.

text.p: Congressman Joe Kennedy, D-Mass, appealed on Thursday to the Federal Communications Commission to investigate the impact of television advertising of liquor on children.

Kennedy, in a letter to FCC chairman Reed Hundt, criticized Seagram Co Ltd for advertising its Crown Royal and Chivas Regal brands in New Hampshire and for its desire to expand into other markets. The Canadian liquor giant began advertising on television in Texas in June.

"Seagram's decision marked for the first break with a voluntary ban on television advertising established in 1948," Kennedy wrote. "With the tolls of alcohol abuse mounting daily in our society, this is no time to abandon the voluntary pledge,"
The congressman also wrote to Seagram Chief Executive Officer Edgar Bronfman, Jr, asking him to suspend the ads. Seagrams officials did not return calls seeking comment.

At least one Boston area television station will not be running the Seagram's ads, but as WBZ-TV Vice President and General Manager Bill Aber explained, the decision had nothing to do with the congressman.

"It is a decades-long policy not to carry advertising for liquor," Aber said. "This is a Westinghouse station and it's been Westinghouse policy since 1947 not to carry any liquor ads. Westinghouse bought CBS and we have continued the same policy."

Seagram spokeswoman Bevin Grove said in a telephone interview there was no immediate reaction to the congressman's letter, but that the company had been considering entering broadcast advertising "for quite some time."
She said the "media landscape has changed" since 1948 and "now we can target our advertising to the adult market."
